title: GhostAction Crosses Paths With PolinRider: Inside the October Escalation
content_md: TL;DR Between Oct. 13 and Oct. 21, 2026, the GhostAction operator pushed 72,000 commits to 23,000 public repositories. 8,000 of them are new victims. 1,382 of the 1,792 compromised accounts had already been used on Oct. 8, so the same stolen tokens keep working. The campaign now ships five payload families. It now also targets developer machines, self-hosted runners, and AWS roles reachable through OpenID Connect (OIDC). One family is a Node.js stealer disguised as a font file and launched by VS Code when a developer opens the git repository. The launcher is the one used by PolinRider, another campaign that hides loaders in developer repos. From Oct. 22 to 26, PolinRider loaders were added to GhostAction commits, which were then force-pushed. Three families install a cron job that runs a script from the command-and-control (C2) server every five minutes. Cleaning the repository does not remove it. The last GhostAction commit we saw was pushed at 04:37 UTC on Oct. 21. All counts in this post are lower bounds: they only include what our feed observed. Times are UTC. Where we left off In our previous post , we described the "Security Audit" wave of Oct. 8 to 12. The operator pushed security-audit.yml to about 30,000 repositories, with a payload that greps the working tree and the full git history for credentials.
